interface: PDZ3 against its natural CRIPT peptide ligand
role: method development substrate; not a pathogen target proposal
feature_encoding: (position index, substituted residue index) for a single substitution
endpoint: peptide binding against a natural ligand
direction: higher DMS_score is better within this assay only
rationale: A peptide-protein interface rather than an antibody-protein one, so the measured endpoint is the kind of interaction this project is trying to design. Small, and singles only.
limitations: None of these is a pathogen target proposal. Spike RBD appears here for method development and is explicitly rejected in the target write-up as a basis for conservation claims.
Every landscape is canonical amino acids on a folded protein domain. None contains a macrocycle, a non-canonical residue or a cyclisation, so none supports a claim about macrocyclic chemistry.

The peptide-binding landscapes mutate the protein side of the interface, not the peptide ligand. They measure how an interface tolerates substitution, which is adjacent to but not the same as designing a binder against a fixed target.
Assay endpoints differ across these landscapes and across the pathogen landscapes. Metrics are never pooled between them.
The measured endpoint is peptide binding against a natural ligand. It is not a macrocycle measurement and establishes nothing about non-canonical chemistry.
